prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1197; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for the claim file. Can you state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just go by "the claimant" for this, if that's fine.

Q: That works. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Houston, heading toward a shopping center. A car came over into my lane while we were both going slow, maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. We hit nose to nose. It didn't feel like a big crash, but my head snapped forward and back.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?

A: No, they didn't. The seatbelt grabbed me pretty hard across the chest, though.

Q: Did you hit your head on anything inside the vehicle?

A: I don't think so. My head just whipped back against the headrest. I remember sitting there for a minute feeling dazed.

Q: Did you get out of the car at the scene or stay inside?

A: I got out, but I was unsteady on my feet. Someone asked if I was okay and I couldn't really remember what I'd said a few seconds earlier.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to the emergency room that evening. They ran a scan and told me I had a concussion. I've had headaches, trouble concentrating, and I get dizzy when I'm reading too long.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?

A: I'm seeing a doctor for follow-up and I've been told to limit screen time and take it easy at work. I'm trying to follow that, but it's been hard.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Just that I want the record to show I'm not trying to exaggerate. I'm doing what the doctors tell me.

Q: Understood. This concludes the statement. Thank you.
